item.title: A 10.22-kg rock used as a Michigan barn doorstop was identified as a new iron meteorite
item.description: In 1939, a meteorite was unearthed on a Michigan farm and innocently pressed into service as a doorstop for many years. It wasn't until 2018, following the fall of another meteorite, that subsequent owners saw its true value. Central Michigan University performed an analysis and confirmed it as a new IIIAB iron meteorite, shedding light on the crucial role of personal specimens in advancing scientific knowledge.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Antarctica’s 2 native flowering plants responded differently to 7 years of warming
item.description: Research on King George Island examined how two native Antarctic plants responded to long-term warming. Antarctic hairgrass displayed reduced hydraulic conductivity and photosynthesis compared to those in natural conditions. In contrast, Antarctic pearlwort increased both its hydraulic conductivity and photosynthetic capacity. This study provided insights into contrasting adaptive strategies of these plants under sustained environmental changes. These findings highlight the need to understand species-specific responses to climate change effects.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Michigan collector's $30 estate sale find turned into a Gertrude Abercrombie artwork worth $1.35 million
item.description: In a stunning turn of events, Gertrude Abercrombie's painting, Alderman Merriam's Shells, was auctioned for $1,352,600 after being found at an estate sale for just $30. Having been lost for 75 years, the piece drew significant attention at Freeman's auction house, far exceeding expectations. A dedicated collector meticulously verified its authenticity, marking a remarkable resurgence for Abercrombie in the contemporary art scene.

item.title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
item.description: In a surprising blunder, US President Donald Trump claimed that 125 million individuals participated in India's presidential election, sparking confusion given Brazil's recent electoral events. His remarks drew attention to his concerns over the integrity of the US electoral system. Social media users quickly slammed the President and highlighted inaccuracies in his understanding of India’s election process.

item.title: Schoolteacher's 128-acre retreat joins wildlife corridor; easement protects forests, wetlands and stream
item.description: Jeanne Paisley, a dedicated schoolteacher, has acquired 128 acres in Richford, New York, driven by her desire to find tranquility and preserve nature. Inspired by a profound childhood event, she has consistently sought to protect our planet's natural beauty. This diverse landscape, which includes forests, fields, and wetlands, plays a crucial role in supporting local wildlife and enhancing the Upper Susquehanna River watershed's water quality.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2005, Oprah Winfrey gave $10M for Houston's Angel Lane; 65 homes and a community center followed
item.description: In 2005, Oprah Winfrey committed $10 million to help create Angel Lane in Houston for hurricane evacuees. The project eventually provided 65 furnished homes to displaced families. Eight years after the first residents moved in, the neighbourhood’s long-promised community center finally opened, offering space for education, workforce development and community services.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 3 million face masks could be used to build 1 km road, Australian study finds
item.description: Engineers at RMIT University have discovered a groundbreaking method to recycle single-use face masks by integrating them into road construction. By blending shredded masks with recycled concrete aggregate, the researchers aim to enhance road materials while tackling the problem of mask waste. Their findings suggest that approximately 3 million masks could be utilized in constructing a one-kilometre, two-lane road.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Lucy Mecklenburgh, Ryan Thomas list £675,000 Cheshire mansion for £1.25 million after lavish makeover
item.description: Lucy Mecklenburgh and Ryan Thomas are seeking a £575,000 uplift after listing their Cheshire mansion for £1.25 million. The couple bought the 3,100 sq ft Bramhall property for £675,000 in 2021 and spent thousands transforming it into a four-storey family home featuring a luxury kitchen, gym, sound studio, garage and generous gardens.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Don Williams paid $1.35 million for Maui land in 1994; court vacates $7 million eminent-domain judgment
item.description: In 1994, Don Williams paid $1.35 million for 1.137 acres near Maui’s Maʻalaea Harbor. More than three decades later, Hawaiʻi’s Intermediate Court of Appeals vacated a Circuit Court judgment awarding $7 million in his long-running eminent-domain case. The appellate court found competing valuation evidence created factual disputes requiring further proceedings over just compensation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: €100 typewriter turns out to be WWII Enigma machine, sold for €45,000 at auction
item.description: A German Enigma machine sold for €100 at a Romanian flea market surprised many when it fetched €45,000 at auction. The machine, thought to be a regular typewriter, was identified by a cryptography professor who recognized its historical significance. After purchasing it, the professor cleaned and repaired the machine to prepare it for auction. This Enigma machine was used during World War II for military communications.

item.title: Why was Kick streamer JohnWhatsGoingOn slapped during Vietnam 7-Eleven livestream?
item.description: While livestreaming from a Vietnam 7-Eleven, streamer JohnWhatsGoingOn found himself in a contentious situation when he recorded an Indian man without permission. The man expressed his discomfort with being filmed, but John continued to record, raising tensions. It culminated in a physical altercation when the man slapped the streamer, who managed to capture the encounter on camera. This incident has ignited a heated online discussion surrounding consent in public filming.

item.title: NitroCamden finally meets StableRonaldo in person after Twitch raid changed his life
item.description: On October 3, 2026, NitroCamden and StableRonaldo connected at ComplexCon after an impactful Twitch raid that drastically altered Camden's streaming journey. What once began as a modest channel with just one viewer exploded overnight, amassing 100,000 followers in 24 hours. While Camden encountered personal hurdles amidst this rapid rise, their meeting represents a pivotal moment, marking the beginning of a promising chapter in his streaming career.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Malena Tudi to address viral claims about her divorce from Nmplol after months away from internet
item.description: Malena Tudi is gearing up for her return to Twitch to clarify misleading narratives surrounding her divorce from Nick 'Nmplol' Polom. She highlighted the significance of dispelling false information that has impacted her personal life and integrity. Tudi aims to approach the situation with care to mitigate any further negative fallout.

item.title: Pewdiepie’s Ajax Ai Model: YouTuber unveils local assistant on Qwen3.5-9B; OpenAI account suspensions loom
item.description: PewDiePie has unveiled Ajax, a smaller AI model designed to run locally through his self-hosted Odysseus workspace. The project follows his claim that OpenAI suspended his account twice during development, with one displayed email citing “distillation.” Built on Alibaba’s Qwen3.5-9B, Ajax aims to handle everyday tasks while offering a less restrictive experience. However, the model remains unfinished, with benchmarks, hardware requirements and downloadable weights yet to be released.
